hook: MISREP 4472514, filed by the 482nd Attack Squadron (482 ATKS), documents three separate UAP encounters observed via Full Motion Video during a 21-hour armed reconnaissance mission over the Arabian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz on July 16, 2020, with all substantive UAP description redacted.
why_it_matters: This report is one of the rare cases where a single mission log contains three formally-catalogued UAP events, each assigned its own standardized observation block with MGRS coordinates and aircraft state data—suggesting the crew treated each as a distinct, reportable incident rather than a recurring sensor artifact. The mission was simultaneously tracking Iranian naval vessels (probable NASER, SAFIR KISH, and HOUDONG fast-attack craft near Bushehr Port), placing the UAP sightings in an operationally sensitive context. The UAP-specific gentext fields are redacted under b)(1) exemptions and classified until March 1, 2045, meaning the actual descriptions of what was seen remain withheld from the public release.
key_findings: Three discrete UAP observations were logged at 1830Z, 1920Z, and 2345Z—each formally recorded as a separate OBSERVATION block with MGRS grid coordinates and aircraft heading, altitude, and airspeed at time of sighting.
All three UAP observations cite FMV (Full Motion Video) as the sole method of observation; no radar or secondary sensor confirmation appears in the visible text.
Weather was recorded as 'NOT A FACTOR' for all three UAP sightings, ruling out atmospheric conditions as a contributing element per the crew's own assessment.

The aircraft was simultaneously conducting ISR on Iranian naval vessels—logging a probable NASER WAP at 0645Z, a probable SAFIR KISH at 1932Z, and a possible HOUDONG docked at Bushehr Port at 2140Z—in the same geographic grid squares where UAP were later observed.

The substantive gentext narratives for all three UAP events are redacted under classification exemptions, with a declassification date of March 1, 2045; only the UAP locations (MGRS grids in the 39RUN/39RVM areas) and the phrase 'OBSERVED AN UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL PHENOMENON' survive in each block.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' and is part of the USCENTCOM MDR 26-0028 release package, making it a direct output of the military UAP reporting pipeline AARO was established to receive.
The mission operated under USCENTCOM in the Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Gulf—a coalition maritime patrol area—though no allied-nation involvement is mentioned in the visible text.
